We have opportunities that you won’t find anywhere else, including hands-on experience, learning opportunities, and the chance to certify in all four major platforms. Whether you want to broaden your knowledge base or narrow your scope and specialize in a specific sector, you can find your opportunity here. Required Skills and Experience • Experience working as a software engineer on complex software projects. • Excellent coding skills and solid development experience (Java, Python, .Net etc.) with debugging and problem-solving skills. • Software development methodologies, with demonstrated experience developing scalable and robust software. • Experienced in relational and NoSQL databases, data mapping, XML/JSON, REST-based web services. • Knowledge of architecture design - Microservices architecture, containers (Docker & k8s), messaging queues. • Deep understanding of OOP and design patterns. We believe in growth, and we’re excited to see what you can bring. At Kyndryl, employee feedback has told us that our number one driver of employee engagement is belonging. That sense of belonging — being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team — is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That’s The Kyndryl Way. Our Be Well programs are thoughtfully designed to support your financial, mental, physical, and social health—because we know that when you feel your best, you do your best. From your very first day, you’ll dive into impactful work that powers the systems our customers rely on every day. You won’t just contribute—you’ll make a difference, tackling meaningful projects that sharpen your skills and fuel your growth. We’re here to champion your journey. With powerful tools to chart your career path, personalized development goals aligned with your ambitions, and continuous feedback to keep you inspired and on track, you’ll have everything you need to thrive and evolve. And through it all, you’ll be part of a culture that values empathy, restless learning, and a devotion to shared success. We want you to thrive here—and we’re committed to helping you do just that. Ready to make an impact? Join us and help shape what’s next. Get Referred! title: Software Engineer
description: Itron is innovating new ways for utilities and cities to manage energy and water. We create a more resourceful world to protect essential resources for today and tomorrow. Join us. Itron Resiliency Solutions is an innovative business unit within Itron focused on solving mission critical problems for utilities through software and AI. Resiliency Solutions offers unique, market leading solutions for front-line worker safety, storm response, excavation damage prevention, construction management, and many more. These software and AI solutions solve end-to-end challenges for the utilities that power our society and are used by the largest and most complex organizations in the world such as National Grid, Southern Company, and Exelon. Itron Resiliency Solutions is a global, diverse team of builders and innovators who tackle previously impossible challenges for our customers. If you have a desire to challenge yourself, solve impactful problems, and work with a passionate and talented team, this is the place. The Emergency Preparedness & Response (EP&R) team builds the systems that keep critical operations running when it matters most. When storms and severe weather threaten communities and infrastructure across the US, our platform enables customers to rapidly procure, mobilize, and manage the workforce needed to respond to and recover from storm damage — often under tight timelines and high-stakes conditions. We are looking for a Principal Engineer who is deeply hands-on, works backward from customer pain points and business needs, and measures success by impact rather than lines of code shipped. You will be the technical anchor of the team: a backend-heavy full-stack engineer who knows our systems inside and out, reasons rigorously about trade-offs, and raises the engineering bar for everyone around you while leading the team toward outcomes that genuinely matter. About the role We're hiring a Software Engineer in Bengaluru to build and run production services. You'll own features end to end — from understanding the problem to shipping, monitoring and fixing what you built — with growing independence and support from senior engineers. Our India engineering team is taking full ownership of core products and growing quickly, including a ground-up rebuild of a customer-critical service. You'll work closely with senior engineers, your Engineering Manager, Product and Customer Support. What you'll own in your first year Own: Own features and services end to end with speed and quality — build, test, release, monitor, fix. Well-scoped problems, then bigger ones. Start with clearly defined work and grow into breaking down ambiguous problems yourself. Design. Write design notes for your features and get them reviewed; contribute to larger designs led by senior engineers. Quality. Write tests, add observability, and take part in on-call so issues are caught before customers see them. Customers. Understand who uses what you build, and learn from support issues what to fix next. Code reviews. Give and receive thoughtful reviews, and help onboard engineers who join after you. What you must bring These are the bar. We can't teach them on the job. Experience: 1–4 years building production software. We level on demonstrated scope, not years alone. You've shipped code that runs in production. Features or services you built, released and supported — not only coursework or prototypes. You are strong at problem solving. You can take an unfamiliar, feature-sized problem, reason through it, and land on a simple, correct solution. You work independently toward a clear goal. Given a clear goal, you figure out the steps, unblock yourself, and ask for help at the right moments. We care how you engineer more than which language you did it in. Technical background You've built production software with a modern stack, such as: Cloud: hands-on with AWS — you've deployed and debugged services running on it. Languages: strong in at least one modern language such as Python, Java or JavaScript/TypeScript. Frameworks: modern service frameworks such as FastAPI, Node.js or equivalents. Databases: solid data modeling and query fundamentals — you can design a schema, use indexes well, and explain why a query is slow and how you'd fix it. Fundamentals: data structures, API design, and the basics of caching and concurrency. Exact tools matter less than depth. Strong experience on an equivalent stack is welcome. What sets great candidates apart Impact you can explain. You can say what changed because of something you built — for users, performance or reliability. One problem you went deep on. A bug, a performance issue or a design where you dug past the surface to understand why. Ownership beyond the ticket. You've fixed what you shipped when it broke, and improved it after release without being asked. Framework mindset: You notice repeated code and turn it into something reusable. Learning speed. You've picked up a new domain, codebase or technology quickly and delivered in it. Curiosity about the user. You've asked why a requirement exists, or suggested a simpler way to solve the user's problem. What we look for in everyone we hire Whatever the role, we hire for six things. Customer obsession. You care who uses what you build and whether it actually helped them. Impact over activity. You measure success by outcomes, not tickets closed or lines written. Honesty. You're specific about your own part in team work, raise problems early, and say what didn't work. Independence. You don't wait to be told every next step. You figure things out with little hand-holding. You will work with leaders who will partner with you in the journey. Passion. Not the word on a resume — the evidence: a side project, a technology you went deep on, something you built because you wanted to. Depth. At least one thing you've built or debugged that you can explain down to the internals and the tradeoffs. Itron is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workforce and providing an authentic workplace experience for all employees. If you are excited about this role but your past experiences don't perfectly align with every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway. In the end, you may be just who we are looking for! The successful candidate's starting wage will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills and experience. Itron is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. If you require an accommodation to apply, please contact a recruiting representative at 1-800-635-5461 or email Accessibility@itron.com. Itron is transforming how the world manages energy, water and city services. Our trusted intelligent infrastructure solutions help utilities and cities improve efficiency, build resilience and deliver safe, reliable and affordable service. With edge intelligence, we connect people, data insights and devices so communities can better manage the essential resources they rely on to live. Join us as we create a more resourceful world: www.itron.com

title: Senior Database Engineer – SQL/NoSQL (Development & Architecture)
description: About the Role We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Senior Database Engineer to take ownership of our database systems, including the development, architecture, optimization, administration, and maintenance of both SQL and NoSQL databases. This is a hands-on technical role combining the responsibilities of a Database Developer, Database Administrator, and Database Architect. The ideal candidate must be capable of designing complex, scalable database architectures from the ground up while also possessing strong programming skills to develop and optimize stored procedures, complex queries, functions, scripts, and other database components. You will work closely with software architects, backend developers, DevOps engineers, and project teams to ensure that our database systems are secure, reliable, highly available, and optimized for performance. Key Responsibilities 1. Database Architecture & Design Design and architect highly scalable, secure, and efficient SQL and NoSQL database solutions for complex enterprise applications. Evaluate project requirements and determine the most appropriate database technologies and architectural approaches. Design logical and physical data models, relational schemas, document structures, relationships, and indexing strategies. Define database architecture for high-volume transactional applications, distributed systems, and microservices. Implement database design principles including normalization, denormalization, partitioning, replication, and sharding where appropriate. Design solutions for high availability, fault tolerance, disaster recovery, and horizontal/vertical scaling. Establish database architecture standards, documentation, and best practices across projects. 2. Database Development & Programming Develop, maintain, and optimize complex SQL queries, stored procedures, functions, triggers, views, and database scripts. Write efficient T-SQL, PL/pgSQL, or equivalent database programming code. Develop database-level logic and data processing routines for complex application requirements. Implement efficient data retrieval, transformation, validation, and manipulation operations. Design and maintain database migration scripts, schema changes, and data correction utilities. Optimize existing database code for performance, maintainability, and reliability. Review database scripts and SQL code developed by other engineers. Troubleshoot complex database programming issues and resolve data inconsistencies. 3. SQL & NoSQL Database Expertise Work extensively with relational databases such as Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL, and MySQL. Design, develop, and maintain NoSQL databases such as MongoDB and Amazon DynamoDB. Understand and apply SQL versus NoSQL architectural patterns based on application requirements. Implement appropriate indexing, query optimization, and data modeling strategies for both relational and non-relational databases. Design efficient document schemas, collections, partition keys, and data access patterns. Work with caching technologies such as Redis where applicable. Evaluate trade-offs involving transactions, consistency, availability, scalability, and performance. 4. Database Administration & Maintenance Manage and maintain existing production, staging, and development database environments. Proactively monitor database health, availability, performance, storage utilization, and resource consumption. Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, deadlocks, locking issues, inefficient queries, and connection problems. Establish and maintain automated database backup, recovery, and disaster recovery procedures. Perform database upgrades, migrations, maintenance, and routine health checks. Implement appropriate database security controls, encryption, access management, and audit logging. Ensure database integrity, consistency, reliability, and data protection. Conduct root cause analysis of database incidents and implement preventive measures. 5. Performance Optimization & Scalability Analyze execution plans, query performance, indexing strategies, and database resource utilization. Optimize database schemas, stored procedures, queries, and data access patterns for improved application performance. Design scalable solutions capable of handling high transaction volumes and increasing data workloads. Implement query optimization, connection pooling, replication, and partitioning strategies where appropriate. Perform database capacity planning and identify opportunities for infrastructure and cost optimization. Recommend architectural improvements to address emerging performance and scalability challenges. 6. Cloud Database Management & Automation Work with cloud-hosted and managed database services, particularly on AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud. Manage services such as Amazon RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, Azure SQL Database, or equivalent platforms. Develop automation scripts using Python, PowerShell, Bash, or similar technologies for database maintenance and operational tasks. Collaborate with DevOps engineers to implement automated database deployments and infrastructure improvements. Integrate database schema changes and migrations into CI/CD pipelines. Support database migration between on-premises, cloud-hosted, and managed database environments. 7. Technical Collaboration & Engineering Standards Collaborate with software architects, backend engineers, and technical leads during solution design and implementation. Participate in architecture discussions and recommend suitable database technologies and designs. Review database architecture and SQL/NoSQL implementations across projects. Define coding standards, database development guidelines, and performance optimization practices. Maintain documentation covering database structures, configurations, dependencies, and recovery procedures. Provide technical guidance and mentorship to software developers on database best practices. Take ownership of complex database-related technical challenges and drive them through resolution. Required Technical Skills Relational Databases (Mandatory) Strong production experience with at least one major relational database: Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL, or MySQL. Expert-level SQL programming and query optimization. Advanced experience with stored procedures, functions, triggers, views, and database scripts. Strong understanding of indexing, execution plans, transactions, locking, concurrency, and performance tuning. Experience designing relational schemas for complex enterprise applications. NoSQL Databases (Mandatory) Hands-on production experience with at least one major NoSQL database, preferably MongoDB or DynamoDB. Strong understanding of NoSQL data modeling, query patterns, indexing, and scalability. Experience designing and optimizing NoSQL databases for real-world application requirements. Understanding of consistency models, partitioning, replication, and distributed data management. Database Architecture (Mandatory) Demonstrated experience independently designing database architectures for medium-to-large or complex applications. Strong understanding of relational and NoSQL architectural patterns. Experience with high-availability, replication, disaster recovery, and scalable database solutions. Ability to evaluate and recommend suitable database technologies based on functional and non-functional requirements. Experience with cloud-hosted database architecture. Database Operations (Mandatory) Production database administration, monitoring, troubleshooting, and maintenance. Database backup and restoration, including recovery testing. Database security, role-based access control, and data integrity. Database performance monitoring and capacity planning. Safe production schema migrations and deployment practices. Programming & Automation Advanced SQL/T-SQL/PL/pgSQL or equivalent database programming skills. Experience with Python, PowerShell, Bash, or similar scripting languages. Experience with Git, version-controlled database scripts, and database deployment automation. Preferred Qualifications 7+ years of relevant professional experience in database engineering, development, architecture, or administration. Strong, verifiable production experience with both SQL and NoSQL technologies. Experience architecting database solutions for enterprise applications, SaaS platforms, or high-volume transactional systems. Experience working with .NET, Node.js, or other backend development ecosystems. Familiarity with microservices architecture, REST/GraphQL APIs, and distributed systems. Knowledge of AWS, Azure, or GCP database services. Experience with database migration, modernization, and performance improvement initiatives. Familiarity with database observability tools and cloud monitoring services. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Key Competencies Strong architectural thinking combined with hands-on programming ability. Excellent analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills. Ability to independently own database-related technical decisions. Strong understanding of application performance and database dependencies. Ability to balance scalability, reliability, security, performance, and cost. Excellent communication, documentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Proactive approach to identifying and preventing production database issues.
